summary: The Foreign Funding Transparency Act requires specific tax-exempt organizations to report information regarding contributions from foreign nationals to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).

affected_groups.effect: Must track and report aggregate foreign contributions and specific contributions from designated foreign countries of concern on their annual IRS information returns, provided they meet certain financial thresholds.
May be required to provide nationality information to recipient organizations.
affected_groups.group: Foreign nationals contributing to tax-exempt organizations

key_provisions: Applies to Section 501(c) tax-exempt organizations with gross receipts of $200,000 or more, or assets of $500,000 or more, in the preceding tax year.
Requires affected organizations filing Form 990 series returns to report the total amount of contributions received from foreign nationals during the tax year.
Requires reporting of contribution amounts received from foreign nationals specifically originating from foreign countries of concern, such as China, Iran, Korea, or Russia.
Allows organizations to rely on a donor's representation of nationality unless the organization knows or should know that the representation is false.
Authorizes the Treasury Secretary to issue regulations on collecting this information from foreign national contributors.
Applies to returns filed for taxable years beginning more than one year after the bill is enacted.
missing_information: The exact definition or list of all countries of concern under section 10612 of the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, beyond the specific mentions of China, Iran, Korea, or Russia in the CRS summary.
The exact definition of a foreign national under section 319(b) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Foreign Funding Transparency Act requires specific tax-exempt organizations to report information regarding contributions from foreign nationals to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a new mandatory reporting mechanism for certain tax-exempt entities regarding foreign financial backing, specifically isolating contributions from designated countries.
